regulation: Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006 Annex (retained in UK law): HIGH FIBRE >=6g/100g or >=3g/100kcal; SOURCE OF FIBRE >=3g/100g or >=1.5g/100kcal; HIGH PROTEIN >=20% of energy from protein; SOURCE OF PROTEIN >=12%; LOW SUGARS <=5g/100g (<=2.5g/100ml liquids); NO ADDED SUGARS = no mono/disaccharides or sugar-used-for-sweetening added. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2006/1924/annex

off_uk_pool.source: Open Food Facts UK pool, 36548 products (data/products/uk_products.parquet); no prices in OFF, so the pool answers 'does the claim match the nutrition', not 'does it cost more'

unclaimed_fibre.note: products that could truthfully carry a 'high fibre' claim but do not: the honest-claim lever sim/optimise.py uses

no_added_sugar.note: NAS is about ADDED sugar; total sugar (e.g. fruit) can stay high legitimately

catalog_price_caveat: 85/96 catalog prices are curator assumptions (price_source 'assumption: ...'); the rest cite a retailer URL. Premiums inherit that uncertainty.
